correctness.rationale: The deterministic greedy simultaneous embeddings of X=P^k and Y=rev(P)^ell have a shared next letter exactly at i+j congruent q-1 mod q. At most k+ell-1 shared steps occur before either input finishes, proving the lower bound (q-1)(k+ell)+1 together with qk and qell. When A,B>=0, the skeleton has q-1 solo steps before first shared step, q-2 between consecutive shared steps, and q-1 after last shared step. Any A X-solo and B Y-solo schedule is feasible; greedy transitions recover solo types uniquely from the resulting word, so distinct output words are in bijection with binomial(A+B,A) schedules. When A or B<0, the shorter input embeds entirely in the longer reverse-period input, giving a unique optimum. Independent set-valued exact SCS dynamic programming computed all distinct shortest words for 27 (q,k,ell) triples (q=2..4; k,ell=1..3), checking both length and count, including q=2 and threshold cases; all agreed. Finite testing supports rather than replaces the all-parameter greedy-skeleton proof.
residual_risks: Own exhaustive language-set verification limited to 27 small parameter triples; reviewed 448-case source dynamic checker without rerunning all sizes.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: published general SCS algorithms treat arbitrary inputs and compute optimum length or enumerate all inclusion-minimal words; they do not give this all-q, unequal-exponent, distinct shortest-output binomial formula. A nearby complete ternary binomial law counts maximal common SUBSEQUENCES, not shortest common SUPERSEQUENCES, and its source provides no bijection between these distinct output families. Arbitrary-power reversal is a structurally distinct claim.

value.rationale: Counting different optimal merged strings is a natural, separate and nontrivial invariant beyond merely computing a shortest possible length or number of alignments. The exact sharp phase transition and all-q, unequal-exponent binomial law solve a complete structured infinite family with a reproducible bijection, useful for string enumeration and merge ambiguity; this is not a renamed textbook LCS formula.

final_claim: For two powers of opposite q-letter permutations X=P^k and Y=reverse(P)^ell, q>=2, k,ell>=1, the shortest common-supersequence length is max(qk,qell,(q-1)(k+ell)+1), and the number of distinct shortest output words is binomial(A+B,A) for A=(q-1)k-ell+1>=0 and B=(q-1)ell-k+1>=0, otherwise 1.
limitations: The count is of distinct output words, not embeddings/alignments or inclusion-minimal but longer supersequences.
